## PDC v0.1.2

The first public build of a folder backup client that is deliberately not a sync engine. You tick the folders you care about, press one button, and each one becomes a plain timestamped archive — `.rar` for a Windows path, `.tar.gz` for a path inside a WSL distribution — inside a folder named after the day. Nothing is mirrored, nothing is written into a proprietary container, and any archiver can open the result years from now.

## New

### One button, plain archives

- Ticking sources and pressing run produces one archive per source in a dated subfolder of the single destination folder you configured; each source reports its own archive path or its own error, so one failure does not hide the other results.
- Windows paths are archived with WinRAR's `rar a -ep1`, so the archive holds the folder's own contents rather than a copy of the drive layout.
- `node_modules` is skipped, which is the difference between a usable archive and a multi-gigabyte one for a front-end project.
- A run writes a full log to `<app dir>/logs/backup-yyyy-MM-dd.log`: the time, the selected source names, and one line per source.

### The archiver is picked per source

- A path is recognised as living inside WSL by its UNC form (`\\wsl$\…`, `\\wsl.localhost\…`) or by being an absolute Linux path, and is then archived with `wsl.exe tar -czf -` instead of `rar`.
- Self-reported paths inside a distribution cannot be `stat`ed by Windows, so existence is checked with `wsl.exe test -e`.
- `/mnt/d/...` is translated through `wslpath -w` and falls back to `rar` on the Windows side.
- A `tar` run that exits with code 1 while every stderr line is a known non-fatal warning (`file changed as we read it`, `socket ignored`, …) still counts as a successful backup.

### Settings that behave like a person set them

- Any number of sources, each with a name and a path, deduplicated by path on save; one destination folder for all of them.
- The source name follows the selected folder only while it still holds the auto-derived value — a name you typed yourself is never overwritten by a later folder change.
- The main window reloads through a broadcast channel the moment settings are saved elsewhere in the app, so the two views never disagree.
- Every source and the destination have an 打开路径 button that opens Explorer at that folder.

### Headless and scheduled runs

- `npm run backup` starts `scripts/run-backup.mjs`, which finds the application executable and runs it with `--backup --config <path>`; `--config` accepts your own configuration file.
- `scripts/auto-backup.bat` is meant to be pointed at by Task Scheduler: it looks for `logs/backup-<yyyy-MM>-*.log` and only runs the backup when the current month has none yet, so a monthly schedule cannot double up.
- The packaging config ships `scripts/` and `backup.config.json` as extra resources, so the scheduled path also works on an installed copy rather than only in the repository.

### Packaging

- electron-builder targets: `nsis` and `portable` on Windows, `dmg` and `zip` on macOS, `AppImage`, `deb` and `rpm` on Linux, all written to `dist-electron/`.
- The application now ships its own icon: a white rounded tile with a stacked archive, transparent outside the tile, exported as `.ico` (7 sizes) and `.png`.

## Notes

- Requires Node `^20.19 || >=22.12`; WinRAR must be installed and `rar` on `PATH` for Windows-path backups, and a WSL distribution for the paths that live inside one.
- Stack: Vue 3 · Vite 8 · Element Plus · Electron 41 · IndexedDB · prettier + eslint (flat config).
